description: Issue #944: LookupCacheService.RefreshAsync<T> lacked the same 'unregistered (non-[CacheLookup]) type must never be written to the cache' bypass its own sibling methods GetAll/GetAllAsync already had as their first check (Bug #112 (2)). Without it, RefreshAsync<T> would proceed to Invalidate/LoadFromDbAsync/SetCache for ANY T, including a type that was never decorated with [CacheLookup] -- and SetCache<T> only sets AbsoluteExpirationRelativeToNow when the type is found in _registry, so an unregistered type's entry gets NO TTL and no working per-type CTS invalidation path, making it effectively immortal in IMemoryCache until process restart or size-based eviction pressure. Reachable in production via WTMContext.RefreshLookupAsync<T>(), which calls svc.GetAttribute(typeof(T)) (returns null for an unregistered type, no guard) and then unconditionally calls svc.RefreshAsync<T>(...) regardless. Forced into kind='security' for the same reason lookupcache943-distributed-refreshasync-acquired-guard-neutralize.json and etl970-cancellation-classification-guard-neutralize.json document: VALID_KINDS in run_mutant.py only recognizes {'security','selftest'} and this is not a runner meta-fixture -- it is not a traditional auth/injection defect, but an unbounded-cache-growth / stale-data-never-expires integrity guard. This mutant changes the guard `if (!_registry.ContainsKey(typeof(T)))` to `if (false)` -- a one-line, compile-preserving change that makes the bypass permanently unreachable, so RefreshAsync<T> proceeds to cache ANY type, registered or not, exactly as the pre-#944 code did.
target_symbol: LookupCacheService.RefreshAsync -- the `if (!_registry.ContainsKey(typeof(T)))` unregistered-type bypass added by #944

Bug #944: RefreshAsync<T> must not write an unregistered (non-[CacheLookup]) type to the cache — such an entry would never expire (SetCache only sets a TTL for registered types) and has no working invalidation path.'. The dry run's own verdict on this first pass (before the pattern was filled in) was UNEXPECTED_RED against the PLACEHOLDER pattern, confirming the harness genuinely evaluated the mutant rather than short-circuiting; the result JSON (<scratch-dir>/lookupcache944-refreshasync-registry-guard-neutralize-result.json) records the same message verbatim. The chosen pattern intentionally excludes the parenthesized/bracketed tail of the message ('(non-[CacheLookup]) type to the cache ...') to avoid needing to escape regex metacharacters unnecessarily -- 'Bug #944: RefreshAsync<T> must not write an unregistered' alone is already unique to this guard's own assertion text and does not match any PROBE_MESSAGES. After filling in the pattern above, two independent invocations of `python3 test/mutants/run_mutant.py --mutant lookupcache944-refreshasync-registry-guard-neutralize` both reported 'VERDICT: KILLED' / 'GATE: PASS'.
